compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The platform verifies one artifact and publishes a different one, and nothing reconciles the two. Pilot execution `intake-83bd3367` pushed three times, all returning commit `37fd44e7a7` against one ledger row. Its second repair fixed a snapshot file, checks passed, and the promoted branch lacks that fix.

`_clean_checkout` at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/checks.py:38` copies the workspace working tree and checks that copy, on the stated basis that it is "exactly what the pull request will carry". The publish path never reads the workspace. `collect_changes` at `services/orchestration/materialization.py:177` reduces it to a `dict[str, str]`, and `commit_and_push` at `adapters/real/git_host.py:120` clones into a temporary directory, writes those files, commits and pushes.

That mapping is lossy. It skips porcelain statuses containing `D` (line 185), so deletions never reach the branch. It reads paths with `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (line 189), so binary files raise. It passes `--no-renames` (line 179), so a rename becomes an add plus a dropped delete, and carries no mode. `repair.py:91`, `repair.py:102` and `implementation.py:196` derive `changed_files` and `applied` from the same mapping, so a repair that only deletes a file reports that it changed nothing.

Three mechanisms then assume one commit per execution, which the repair loop violates. `mediator.py:115` targets its `SideEffectRef` on `f"{repo}:{request.branch}"` while `side_effect_key` at `services/coordination/idempotency.py:39` hashes only task, execution, operation and target. All three git hosts return early on a prior `execution_id` trailer, at `adapters/real/git_host.py:127`, `adapters/real/local_git_host.py:124` and `adapters/mock/git_host.py:98`. The activity at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/pull_request.py:287` re-materializes at the previous push's head, so `_ensure_checkout` at `materialization.py:145` runs `reset --hard` and `clean -fd` over the first repair's edits.

## Approach

Publish the workspace itself rather than a reconstruction of it.

The workspace is already a git checkout with an authenticated remote, because `materialization.py:88` takes `remote_url_for` from `build_git_host(resolved).source_location`, which `adapters/real/git_host.py:81` returns as the URL the adapter pushes with. It stages its change, and the adapter commits that staged tree in the workspace and pushes the branch. The temporary clone and the file mapping go away, so deletions, renames, binary content and modes survive because git carries them. Reporting moves to a `changed_paths` helper listing every changed path including deletions. `_hash_changes` at `implementation.py:82` goes too, because the staged tree hash digests the same content while covering deletions, binary files and modes, so `diff_hash` carries it.

Content addressing replaces the execution-scoped dedup. `git write-tree` yields a hash that differs per repair attempt and repeats for a retry of one attempt, which is the idempotency the trailer search was reaching for, without a counter. The adapter replays when the remote head's tree matches the staged tree, so a retry after a push that already landed is safe rather than a non-fast-forward rejection. The activity stages through the materializer, `build_commit_request` carries the tree on `CommitRequest.tree`, and the mediator targets its ref on `f"{repo}:{branch}@{tree}"`.

Re-materialization then resolves itself, because the head the workflow carries forward becomes the workspace head and `_ensure_checkout` takes its early return at `materialization.py:151`. An arbitrary base still works, since the workspace is materialized once and afterwards only moves forward by local commits. After pushing, the activity checks that the remote branch head equals the workspace head and that the workspace is clean, logging both heads when they diverge.

The commit disables signing and hooks for the reason ADEVX-130 established. Adding a ledger discriminator while keeping the mapping was rejected, because the trailer search would still decline the push.

## Scope

Per-file reasons are in this ticket's file impact. `docs/change-publication.md` and `tests/unit/test_commit_publish.py` are new.

## Grounded assumptions

- `collect_changes` has four production callers, at `materialization.py:199`, `repair.py:91`, `repair.py:102` and `implementation.py:196`, plus two test consumers, the `_FakeMaterializer` stub at `tests/unit/test_implementation_activity.py:54` and `test_collect_changes_builds_a_commit_request_with_the_execution_trailer` at `tests/integration/test_workspace_materialization.py:240`. `materialization.py:199` builds the commit from content and `implementation.py:211` hashes it for `diff_hash`, both of which the staged tree replaces. The rest need paths alone, and both test consumers move to the new contract.
- The sequence gate does not block the extra pushes. `_admissible` at `services/coordination/sequencing.py:30` admits a sequence ahead of the current one, and the pilot carried 202, 205 and 207.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A file deleted in the workspace is absent from the published tree, verified by `tests/unit/test_commit_publish.py`.
- [ ] A file renamed in the workspace appears only at its new path, verified by the same module.
- [ ] A file whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 is published unchanged, verified by the same module.
- [ ] A file made executable keeps that mode in the published tree, verified by a test reading `git ls-tree`.
- [ ] Two staged changes in one execution produce two distinct commits on the branch, verified by a test counting the branch commits.
- [ ] Publishing an unchanged staged tree a second time reports `replayed` without pushing, verified by a unit test.
- [ ] A publish retried after the remote already holds the staged tree reports `replayed` rather than raising, verified by a unit test.
- [ ] Two different staged trees in one execution produce two different `SideEffectRef` targets, verified by a mediator test.
- [ ] A workspace with no staged difference creates no commit, verified by a staging unit test.
- [ ] `bounded_task_pipeline` returns the no-changes outcome when staging reports no difference, verified by a pipeline test.
- [ ] A workspace whose config sets `commit.gpgsign` with a failing `pre-commit` hook is still committed, verified by a test publishing against such a repository.
- [ ] A re-materialization at the previous push's head preserves uncommitted edits, verified by `tests/integration/test_workspace_materialization.py`.
- [ ] The activity raises when the remote branch head differs from the workspace head after pushing, verified by a unit test.
- [ ] The activity raises when the workspace is not clean after committing, verified by a unit test.
- [ ] A post-push verification failure logs both heads, verified by a unit test asserting on `caplog`.
- [ ] `changed_paths` reports a file the agent deleted, verified by a test over `apply_ci_repair`.
- [ ] `diff_hash` carries the staged tree hash, verified by a test over the implementation activity.
- [ ] `collect_changes` no longer appears in the repository, verified by a repository-wide search returning no match.
- [ ] `docs/change-publication.md` states that the checked tree is the published tree, verified by reading the file.
- [ ] `docs/change-publication.md` names the post-push verification enforcing that invariant, verified by reading the file.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live run of the pilot ticket through at least one repair cycle promotes a pull request whose head passes the checks the platform reported.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the pilot runs the shipped workflow against the client repository over a deployment's Temporal path
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
- [ ] The full test suite passes.
